entities.name: PA delays specialty therapy
observations: A 2023 systematic review of 44 studies found prior authorization associated with significant delays in specialty-drug initiation; long-term clinical-outcome evidence remained limited.

entities.name: Cost sharing abandonment
observations: Higher cost sharing was associated with medication abandonment, reduced initiation and persistence, and higher discontinuation; abandonment reached 75% for some specialty drugs, while MPR/PDC findings were inconsistent.

entities.name: Step therapy harm pathway
observations: A narrative review reported that payer-mandated step therapy can require poorly tolerated or clinically unsuitable drugs, causing treatment delays, discontinuations, and possible adverse events; protocols may not follow guidelines.

entities.name: Unequal PA exposure
observations: In a retrospective gynecologic-oncology cohort of 1,406 patients, 23% experienced prior authorization; occurrence differed by insurance and race/ethnicity, establishing differential exposure but not definitive differential clinical harm.

entities.name: RTPB mitigation
observations: A real-time prescription-benefit intervention showed higher fill rates when patients selected an alternative than when retaining the original prescription (68% vs 59%) and produced average monthly copay savings of $27.77; clinical adverse-event reduction was not shown.

entities.name: PA workflow burden
observations: An observational study across eight community practices identified information-transfer gaps, incompatible formats, outdated technology, workarounds, and care consequences; proposed mitigations included real-time formulary data, alternatives, and EHR-integrated electronic prior authorization.
